title: Fallback LLM Operating Rules
purpose: Structured form of .ai/entrypoints/fallback-contract.md's numbered rules, for a session that can only reach one rulepack file and needs the fallback rules machine-checkable rather than prose-only.

rules.statement: If any .ai/ source file is unavailable, unreadable, or skipped, say so explicitly and state that the fallback contract is now the controlling instruction set, rather than proceeding silently on partial context.
Assign or confirm a REQ-### id before work begins. Do not begin implementation work under a fallback session with no id at all.
State the minimum access scope for the task before inspecting files.
Inspect only files needed for the active requirement. Do not scan the whole repository unless the task cannot be completed safely without it.
Do not read or expose .env, .env.*, private keys, certificates, credentials, database files, logs, build artifacts, dependency folders, cache directories, or anything listed in .ai/.ignore.
Do not modify unrelated files, unrelated deployment scripts, unrelated infrastructure, generated dependency folders, secrets, credentials, or local environment files.
Make the smallest safe, maintainable change. Preserve existing behavior unless it conflicts with the active requirement.
Do not claim completion if validation was skipped or could not be run in this session. State explicitly why it was not run, rather than implying it passed.
Final output includes requirement id and status, files changed, validation performed, documentation/changelog status, known risks or follow-ups, a commit-entry sentence, and pull-request information.
Do not fabricate the contents of an .ai/ file that could not be read. Report it missing and proceed under this rulepack instead of guessing its content.
